Step 2: the directions label the modes themselves — 'Als Haarmaske: auf das nasse Haar auftragen, 3 Minuten einwirken lassen und gründlich ausspülen' has a stated contact time and a rinse and qualifies; 'Als Leave-in-Pflege … nicht ausspülen' fails the rinse conjunct; 'Auch als Over-Night-Pflege verwendbar' is leave-on and falls under the charter's overnight exclusion for that mode. Step 3: exactly one mode qualifies → mode-scoped classification. Charter F1 names Balea Aqua Hyaluron 3 in 1 as a live boundary case that is eligible mode-scoped.

tailMarker.anomalyNote: No §3.1 anomaly. The marker at 9 in a 15-entry list demotes Isoamyl Laurate @10, Behentrimonium Chloride @11 and Cetrimonium Chloride @12 — so this formula's second and third cationic species are both non-contributing, and the credited segment is humectant-led rather than cationic-led. That is the structural fact that makes it the D5 anchor product.  ||  PLAUSIBILITY ASSESSMENT (R2, §3.1.1, added under v0.2): PLAUSIBLE. CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2 and DISTEAROYLETHYL HYDROXYETHYLMONIUM METHOSULFATE @4, with the humectant cluster @3/@5/@6/@7, all outrank PARFUM @9; conventional O/W emulsion with AQUA @1. The second and third cationics (BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @11, CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @12) sit below the marker - an ordinary tail demotion, recorded as a counter-signal. HELIANTHUS ANNUUS HYBRID OIL @8 is the tail_index - 1 species and is excluded from carrying a structural signal (R3); it is the only lipid, so S3 fails either way.

weightPotential.evidenceScope: Formula-only, above-tail ranks 1–8 (marker PARFUM @9, resolved and plausible on all three §3.1.1 limbs); an ingredient-informed matching prior, not a prediction of visible finish.
weightPotential.rationale: CHANGED under v0.3 (E4, applied uniformly per E6, 2026-09-14): `moderate` → `low`. E4 deleted the structural fatty-alcohol conjunct from the leanness test and E6 rules the restated test applies uniformly across the cohort. All three remaining conjuncts are positively observed here: no R4b heavy lipid above the marker (HELIANTHUS ANNUUS HYBRID OIL @8 is a mid/light plant oil), no occlusive silicone stack (no silicone at any rank), and a single cationic species above the tail (DISTEAROYLETHYL HYDROXYETHYLMONIUM METHOSULFATE @4). The v0.2 record called this the third cohort product 'whose lean architecture is refused `low` on the rank cut alone'. It is refused no longer. One caveat travels with the value and is recorded rather than smoothed over: conjunct 3 holds on the above-tail segment, and this formula carries two further cationics below the marker (AP-09-CATIONICSCOPE). E2 ceiling: weight deposition potential, never measured finish.
evidenceSignals: CONJUNCT 1 — no R4b heavy lipid above the marker: SATISFIED. HELIANTHUS ANNUUS HYBRID OIL @8 is the formula's only lipid; lexicon family 3 places conventional plant triglycerides in the MID band and reserves heavy for butters, Ricinus, petrolatum, hydrogenated fats and lanolin, so it is R4a and cannot carry a heavy-lipid core. No butter, hydrogenated fat or occlusive hydrocarbon at ANY rank of the 15-entry list: the conjunct holds on the full list

CONJUNCT 2 — no occlusive silicone stack above the tail: SATISFIED, absolutely. No silicone species at any rank, consistent with (but established independently of) the 'ohne Mikroplastik und wasserlösliche rein synthetische Polymere' positioning

CONJUNCT 3 — a single cationic species: SATISFIED on the above-tail segment. DISTEAROYLETHYL HYDROXYETHYLMONIUM METHOSULFATE @4 is the only S1-family species above PARFUM @9. BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @11 and CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @12 are a second and third cationic on the full list and are demoted by the marker — the same structural fact that makes this the D5 anchor product (a humectant-led rather than cationic-led credited segment) also carries the leanness conjunct. See AP-09-CATIONICSCOPE

COUNTING SCOPE, the material caveat on this call: conjunct 3 holds because BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @11 and CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @12 sit below the marker. On the full list this formula runs THREE cationic species — more than #07, where the same caveat costs one species. §9.2 counts the conjunct on the above-tail segment, as it counts every other term in that section, and its own [judgment call — review] marks that counting scope as this standard's unruled addition, first in line for calibration (§15, §18.2). A reviewer counting on the full list would hold this record at `moderate`. Recorded, not smoothed over: AP-09-CATIONICSCOPE.

WHY-NOT-ADJACENT on conjunct 1: were HELIANTHUS ANNUUS HYBRID OIL @8 read as R4b rather than R4a, conjunct 1 would fail and the value would be `moderate`. The lexicon settles it — family 3 lists sunflower oil with the plant triglycerides and places conventional plant triglycerides in the mid band — so this is not a live alternative reading, unlike the counting-scope question above.

§9.2 conflict fallback checked and NOT engaged in either direction: no `high` value exists to be contradicted, and no lightness positioning was used to reach `low` — the pack's claims are 'geschmeidiges und glänzendes Haar' and the Mikroplastik statement, neither of which is a lightness or a richness claim. `weight_high_conflict` cannot fire on a `low` value.

adjudicationPoints.title: `weight_potential: low` rests on the above-tail counting scope — this formula runs three cationics on the full list (the cohort's strongest instance; see also AP-07-CATIONICSCOPE)
adjudicationPoints.body: E4's leanness test requires 'a single cationic species', and §9.2 counts it on the ABOVE-TAIL segment. Here DISTEAROYLETHYL HYDROXYETHYLMONIUM METHOSULFATE @4 is the only S1-family species above PARFUM @9, so the conjunct holds — but BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @11 and CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @12 are a second and third cationic on the full list, demoted by an early marker in a 15-entry list. The other two conjuncts are scope-independent: no lipid above mid band and no silicone at ANY rank. So the entire `low` call turns on conjunct 3's counting scope, which §9.2's own [judgment call — review] names as this standard's unruled addition and puts first in line for the calibration set. Two observations that make this record the sharpest case. FIRST, the same marker cut is what makes this the D5 anchor product — the tail demotion of the second and third cationics is exactly why the credited segment reads humectant-led rather than cationic-led — so one rank cut is now carrying two of the record's headline findings. That is not double counting in the §6 rule 1 sense (one observation, two fields, not one observation read as two instances of richness), but it does mean a single reading of §3.1 moves both. SECOND, a formula running three deposition species is precisely what E4's own reasoning describes as NOT structurally lean ('a formula running one deposition species is structurally lean in a way a formula running three is not'), and this formula runs three — just not above the marker. WHAT NICK DECIDES: nothing today; the value is recorded as the standard produces it, at `moderate` confidence, which is the honest statement that a neighbouring value is reachable on a rule reading. If the calibration set moves the counting scope to the full list, this record and #07 return to `moderate` while #08 and #12 keep `low`.
